title: Nitrate in a river: how often over the standard?
intro: Illustrative data, made up for this book. Twenty-four monthly nitrate concentrations (mg/L as N) in a river. Concentrations are skewed and positive, so a lognormal model is fitted. The drinking-water standard is 10 mg/L: P(X > 10) is how often a sample would exceed it; the 0.95 quantile is a high-end concentration.
